purpose: The empirical constraint model an evasive attacker on NSL-KDD must obey. It holds no mutation and no search: a consumer reads the roles, the knobs and the constraints from here and does the moving itself.

roles.direct: The attacker sets it by choosing its own behaviour.
roles.derived: The sensor recomputes it from the connection log; reachable only as a joint consequence of behaviour.
roles.fixed: Attack semantics or a definitional invariant pins it; changing it destroys the attack or the plausibility.

effects.dilute_toward_background: A ratio over a fixed 2 s window; slowing down shrinks the attacker's share of it, so the value drifts toward the ambient traffic mix instead of falling with the rate.
effects.near_invariant: Computed over a 100-connection window rather than a time span, so slowing down barely moves it.
effects.unchanged: The knob does not touch it.
effects.unspecified: The research report's §4 gives no direction and this project will not guess one.

support.synthesis: The research report marks it as its own reasoning.

duration.why: The attacker adds latency; increase-only and bounded by what the sensor ever observed.
duration.citation: Apruzzese et al., IEEE TETCI 4(4), 2020, pp. 427-439

protocol_type.why: It decides which services and flags are admissible at all.

service.why: Constrained by the protocol, and r2l attacks are service-defined.

flag.why: TCP termination status is an outcome of the connection, not a field the attacker writes.
flag.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

src_bytes.why: The attacker pads the request with junk data; increase-only and bounded.
src_bytes.citation: Apruzzese et al., IEEE TETCI 4(4), 2020, pp. 427-439

dst_bytes.why: The r2l victim server decides how much it answers; only a botnet attacker owns both ends.
dst_bytes.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

land.why: Definitional invariant: source host and port equal destination host and port.
land.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

wrong_fragment.why: Definitional for fragmentation dos (teardrop) and zero for r2l.
wrong_fragment.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

urgent.why: Settable via the URG pointer, but non-zero values are conspicuous.
urgent.citation: Pierazzi et al., IEEE S&P 2020, pp. 1332-1349

hot.why: The payload decides how many hot indicators the session touches.
hot.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

num_failed_logins.why: This is the guess_passwd signal itself; zeroing it removes the attack.
num_failed_logins.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

logged_in.why: Whether the login succeeded follows from the credentials the payload carries.
logged_in.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

num_compromised.why: Counted from compromised-condition indicators the payload triggers.
num_compromised.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

root_shell.why: Whether a root shell was obtained is the u2r payload's own result.
root_shell.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

su_attempted.why: Whether `su root` was attempted is part of the payload.
su_attempted.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

num_root.why: Counted from root accesses the payload performs.
num_root.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

num_file_creations.why: Counted from file-creation operations the payload performs.
num_file_creations.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

num_shells.why: Counted from shell prompts the payload obtains.
num_shells.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

num_access_files.why: Counted from accesses to access-control files the payload performs.
num_access_files.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

num_outbound_cmds.why: Degenerate: identically zero, so it carries no information to perturb.
num_outbound_cmds.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

is_host_login.why: Whether the login belongs to the host list is a property of the account used.
is_host_login.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

is_guest_login.why: Whether the login is a guest account is a property of the account used.
is_guest_login.citation: Lin, Shi, Xue, IDSGAN, PAKDD 2022, arXiv:1809.02077 (Table 1, verified)

count.why: Connections to the same host in a fixed 2 s window; falls as the attacker slows down.
count.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

srv_count.why: Connections to the same service in a fixed 2 s window; falls as the attacker slows down.
srv_count.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

serror_rate.why: SYN-error ratio over the 2 s same-host window; tied to `flag`.
serror_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

srv_serror_rate.why: SYN-error ratio over the 2 s same-service window; tied to `flag`.
srv_serror_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

rerror_rate.why: REJ-error ratio over the 2 s same-host window; tied to `flag`.
rerror_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

srv_rerror_rate.why: REJ-error ratio over the 2 s same-service window; tied to `flag`.
srv_rerror_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

same_srv_rate.why: Same-service share of the 2 s same-host window; moves only through service spread.
same_srv_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

diff_srv_rate.why: Different-service share of the 2 s same-host window; moves only through service spread.
diff_srv_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

srv_diff_host_rate.why: Different-host share of the 2 s same-service window; rises with host spread.
srv_diff_host_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_count.why: Counted over 100 connections to the same host, a window built to defeat a slow attacker.
dst_host_count.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_srv_count.why: Counted over 100 connections to the same service, so slowing down does not move it.
dst_host_srv_count.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_same_srv_rate.why: Same-service share of the 100-connection host window; moves through service spread.
dst_host_same_srv_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_diff_srv_rate.why: Different-service share of the 100-connection host window; moves through service spread.
dst_host_diff_srv_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_same_src_port_rate.why: Same-source-port share of the 100-connection host window; falls under randomisation.
dst_host_same_src_port_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_srv_diff_host_rate.why: Different-host share of the 100-connection service window; rises with host spread.
dst_host_srv_diff_host_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_serror_rate.why: SYN-error ratio over the 100-connection host window; follows from the outcomes.
dst_host_serror_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_srv_serror_rate.why: SYN-error ratio over the 100-connection service window; follows from the outcomes.
dst_host_srv_serror_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_rerror_rate.why: REJ-error ratio over the 100-connection host window; follows from the outcomes.
dst_host_rerror_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_srv_rerror_rate.why: REJ-error ratio over the 100-connection service window; follows from the outcomes.
dst_host_srv_rerror_rate.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

inter_connection_interval.description: Seconds between the attacker's successive connections; the report's lambda.
inter_connection_interval.rationale: Counts over a fixed 2 s window fall with the rate; ratios over the same window do not, they dilute toward the ambient background; the 100-connection host windows were built precisely to stay invariant to this.
inter_connection_interval.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

count.basis: raw count in a fixed 2 s window

srv_count.basis: raw count in a fixed 2 s window

srv_diff_host_rate.basis: the report's §4 does not give this ratio a direction

dst_host_count.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_srv_count.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_same_srv_rate.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_diff_srv_rate.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_same_src_port_rate.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_srv_diff_host_rate.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_serror_rate.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_srv_serror_rate.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_rerror_rate.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

dst_host_srv_rerror_rate.basis: window is 100 connections, not a time span

host_spread.description: How many distinct destination hosts the attacker's connections are spread over; the report's H.
host_spread.rationale: Spreading the same work over more hosts thins every per-host window and raises the different-host shares.
host_spread.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

count.basis: fewer connections land on any one host

srv_count.basis: the same service is still targeted everywhere

srv_diff_host_rate.basis: same-service connections now reach more hosts

dst_host_srv_diff_host_rate.basis: same-service connections now reach more hosts

service_spread.description: How many distinct services or destination ports the attacker touches; the report's S.
service_spread.rationale: Touching more services moves weight out of the same-service share and into the different-service share.
service_spread.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

same_srv_rate.basis: same-service share of the 2 s window

diff_srv_rate.basis: different-service share of the 2 s window

dst_host_same_srv_rate.basis: same-service share of the 100-connection host window

dst_host_diff_srv_rate.basis: different-service share of the 100-connection host window

source_port_reuse.description: How often the attacker reuses the same source port; lowering it means source-port randomisation.
source_port_reuse.rationale: The 100-connection host window records the same-source-port share, so randomising the port lowers it.
source_port_reuse.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

dst_host_same_src_port_rate.basis: same-source-port share of the 100-connection host window

byte_padding.description: Junk data appended to the attacker's own request.
byte_padding.rationale: Adding random junk data does not alter the underlying logic; excessive increases generate anomalous Flows.
byte_padding.citation: Apruzzese et al., IEEE TETCI 4(4), 2020, pp. 427-439

src_bytes.basis: the attacker writes these bytes itself

added_latency.description: Extra delay held inside a single connection.
added_latency.rationale: Evasion by increasing flow duration through a small latency; flow collectors cap the maximum duration.
added_latency.citation: Apruzzese et al., IEEE TETCI 4(4), 2020, pp. 427-439

duration.basis: the attacker holds the connection open

couplings.note: Rejected. The two rates do not partition one window: `same_srv_rate` is the same-service share of the 2 s same-host window while `diff_srv_rate` behaves as a count of distinct other services over the same denominator, so the sum is usually far below 1 and sometimes above it. An attacker model must not treat `diff_srv_rate` as `1 - same_srv_rate`.
Rejected, and more severely than its 2 s twin: the two host-based rates are computed over two different 100-connection windows (same host, same service), so they have no reason to sum to 1.

Rejected. The two counts are not nested: `dst_host_count` counts inside the last 100 connections to the same host and `dst_host_srv_count` inside the last 100 connections to the same service. Verified against the raw KDDTrain+ lines.

couplings.predicted_by: this project, the 2 s mirror of the ordering the report predicts for the 100-connection windows
couplings.note: Rejected, for the same reason as its host-based twin: `count` is a same-host window and `srv_count` a same-service one.

Rejected as a hard constraint although it very nearly holds: the residual sits inside the rounding slack for most Flows but its p99 is two orders of magnitude outside it, again because numerator and denominator come from two different windows.

couplings.predicted_by: this project, fitted after the report's four predictions were measured
couplings.note: Accepted: the only rate identity the Pool supports. It is the usable replacement for the rejected partition, and it is what forces `same_srv_rate` to move whenever behaviour moves `count` or `srv_count`. Weaker on KDDTest+, see measured.test.
Accepted exactly, in the Pool and in KDDTest+. The feature carries no information, so perturbing it is a wasted move.

flag_fixes_error_rates.statement: `flag` fixes the error-rate family: a Flow cannot keep flag=S0 and drop serror_rate, nor keep REJ and drop rerror.
flag_fixes_error_rates.citation: KDD Cup 1999 task description (Lee & Stolfo, ACM TISSEC 3(4), 2000)

duration.citation: Apruzzese et al., IEEE TETCI 4(4), 2020, pp. 427-439

src_bytes.citation: Apruzzese et al., IEEE TETCI 4(4), 2020, pp. 427-439

deviations_from_research_report.subject: urgent
deviations_from_research_report.why: The role vocabulary has no `implausible` value, and the report itself removes the feature by Pierazzi's plausibility constraint. The Pool agrees: `urgent` is zero in 99.99% of Flows, so any non-zero value is conspicuous.

deviations_from_research_report.subject: dst_bytes
deviations_from_research_report.report: r2l: derived; dos: direct in botnet settings
deviations_from_research_report.why: The botnet scope condition does not hold in NSL-KDD: dos here targets a third-party victim that decides its own response, so the attacker does not own the far endpoint.

deviations_from_research_report.subject: content features under dos
deviations_from_research_report.report: IDSGAN Table 1 frees the content block for dos
deviations_from_research_report.why: Nine of the twelve content features are identically zero across every dos Flow of the Pool; writing non-zero values there asserts application-layer activity that never happened. Measured exceptions are recorded under category_signatures.dos.

deviations_from_research_report.subject: coupling identities
deviations_from_research_report.report: §4 predicts four hard couplings from the published definitions
deviations_from_research_report.model: three of the four are rejected on the Pool's own evidence
deviations_from_research_report.why: `count`/`srv_count` and `dst_host_count`/`dst_host_srv_count` are not nested: each pair is computed over two parallel windows (same host, same service). See couplings for the measured violation rates.
